title: progressive-fidelity-tool-orchestration-for-mobile-sdks-prd-notes
body:
Context and motivation:

Mobile clients (React Native, Android, iOS) are a critical growth surface for customers embedding LLM features. Mobile networks are highly variable: ephemeral bandwidth drops, latency spikes, and application backgrounding require the Hosted API to be resilient and to expose ergonomics that allow clients to display progressively improving results rather than blocking on a single high-fidelity response.

Problem statement:
- Current hosted streaming surfaces push a monolithic result or a raw incremental token stream with no first-class notion of staged tool invocations or fidelity tiers.
- Client SDKs must currently implement ad-hoc heuristics to display partial answers and retry tool calls when connectivity returns.
- Large tool outputs (search results, web fetches, image generation metadata) create spikes in token cost and latency; clients need a way to show a low-cost preview then upgrade to full fidelity if the network and policy allow it.

Goals:
- Provide a server-driven, client-negotiable progressive fidelity protocol for streaming responses that includes: lightweight preview frames, staged tool invocation markers, and an explicit upgrade flow.
- Make SDK ergonomics simple for mobile developers: default safe UI primitives, automatic backoff, and a small set of events to drive UI state.
- Preserve safety and determinism for tool calling: ensure ordered tool execution semantics, idempotency keys, and clear failure semantics when upgrades fail.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full server-side rollouts / experiment framework (this PRD focuses on API surface and client patterns).
- Not prescribing exact UI — we provide primitives and examples only.

User stories:
1) As a mobile product engineer I want the SDK to emit a "preview" result within 150–400ms so the UI can show progress while the model computes a full result.
2) As a developer I want tool outputs (e.g., browser fetch) to be annotated as "deferred" so the client can choose to fetch higher fidelity when on Wi‑Fi.
3) As an SRE I want streaming metrics that break down preview vs final tokens and tool invocation success/failure counts.

High-level solution sketch:
- Introduce the Progressive Fidelity Stream (PFS): a compact framed stream over existing streaming endpoints. Frames include: PREVIEW, TOOL_INTENT, TOOL_PULSE, UPGRADE_OFFER, FULL_COMMIT, ERROR, HEARTBEAT.
- Each frame is a small JSON envelope (single line) with a type, sequence_id, optional schema tag, and payload (payload can be compressed/trimmed). Servers send PREVIEW frames early (model-first pass or heuristic summary).
- TOOL_INTENT frames declare that the model is requesting a tool invocation (tool id, args hash, idempotency_key). TOOL_PULSE frames are tool output previews (truncated structured output). FULL_COMMIT arrives when the model/tool pipeline completes and contains canonical structured output or a pointer (artifact id) if too big.
- Clients can respond via a short control channel (out-of-band) to request UPGRADE for a sequence_id, indicating willingness to accept full fidelity (billing implications surfaced).

API examples (pseudo):
Server streaming chunk (sse/ws/HTTP chunked) line-delimited JSON:
{"type":"PREVIEW","seq":1,"schema":"summary.v1","payload":"Chef recommends starting with oil in pan..."}
{"type":"TOOL_INTENT","seq":2,"tool":"web_fetch","args_hash":"sha256:abcd","idempotency_key":"rid-1234-a"}
{"type":"TOOL_PULSE","seq":3,"tool":"web_fetch","payload_preview":"(top 3 hits) 1) recipe.com, 2) blog.x, 3) reddit thread"}
{"type":"UPGRADE_OFFER","seq":4,"cost_delta":"+0.12 tokens","artifact_hint":"maybe-large"}

Client control (HTTP POST to /v1/upgrade)
{"sequence_ids": [2,3], "accept_cost": true, "auth": "session-token"}

Server final commit arrives as FULL_COMMIT with structured JSON payload or artifact id:
{"type":"FULL_COMMIT","seq":5,"schema":"web_fetch.v2","artifact_id":"artifact://rid/8362","signature":"sig.."}

SDK ergonomics (mobile-focused guidance):
- React Native SDK: provide a small "ProgressiveResponse" object with event listeners: onPreview, onToolIntent, onToolPulse, onUpgradeOffer, onCommit, onError. Default behavior: emit preview to UI, buffer pulses, surface upgrade offer to developer through a single callback.
  - Built-in helper: showPreviewThenCommit(previewRenderer, commitRenderer, options) that handles debouncing UPGRADE if network fast.
- Native Android/iOS (Kotlin/Swift): similar primitives; ensure callbacks are delivered on main thread and expose cancel/terminate to respect app backgrounding.
- Go / server-side SDK: provide both synchronous helper that auto-accepts upgrade when network is good and a streaming iterator style for explicit control.

Telemetry and metrics:
- Surface the following at route/model level: preview_latency_p50/p95, upgrade_accept_rate, tool_intent_count, tool_success_rate, average_cost_delta_for_upgrades, artifact_fetch_errors.
- Tracing: every PFS sequence_id should be correlated with trace id and tool invocation span(s).

Failure modes and policies:
- If client requests UPGRADE but network breaks before commit, server must persist upgrade state for up to 2 minutes and allow retry by idempotency_key. If no retry, server rolls back and emits ERROR with rollback_reason:"client_timeout".
- If tool invocation fails (rate limit, downstream error), TOOL_PULSE should indicate partial result + failure_code and server should still send a PREVIEW-derived fallback.
- Large artifacts: prefer artifact pointers (artifact://) with signed short-lived URLs for fetch; do not inline megabytes into stream.

Security and safety:
- Idempotency and tool authorization: TOOL_INTENT frames carry idempotency_key and caller-permission scope. Private or privileged tools require an additional signature step in control channel (server requests short-lived attestation).
- Privacy: PREVIEW frames should be sanitized to avoid leaking PII in initial previews; add server-side hygiene checks flagged in telemetry.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (alpha): limited to internal SDKs and a small set of customers; server default sends PREVIEW but UPGRADE only when client explicitly opts in.
- Stage 2 (beta): open to self-serve customers with console toggle; telemetry dashboard for upgrade economics.
- Stage 3 (GA): enable by default with conservative preview heuristics, billing docs updated.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should PREVIEW be? model-first pass summaries vs dedicated cheap model for preview. (TODO: perf experiment RID-8279)
- Billing UX: how to show potential cost before user accepts upgrade on mobile? small modal vs passive indicator.
- Tool orchestration semantics: should TOOL_INTENT commit immediately on server or wait for explicit client acceptance for tools that are expensive / external? Proposed default: commit server-side for idempotent low-cost tools, require client upgrade for heavy tools.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: prototype server stream framing and client event API (owner: Marcus Lee, ETA: 3 weeks).
- Research: run 2 experiments comparing model-first preview vs cheap summarizer (owner: Samir, ETA: 4 weeks).
- Product: draft console toggle and billing language (owner: Elena García, ETA: 2 weeks).
- SRE/Observability: add preview/fidelity metrics to per-route dashboard and trace hooks (owner: Jordan Park, ETA: 3 weeks).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and focused on the mobile UX constraints; I expect the serving runtime folks to push back on persistence windows and idempotency guarantees.
- Please flag any places where the protocol introduces significant complexity in existing streaming infra (e.g., stateful upgrade windows).

Rough mockup links / references: see linked_artifacts above and quick prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/tree/progressive-fidelity-proto
